researcher: Codex parallel release159-multan-shared research, integrated by Codex

sources.title: Human History Map civilization index
sources.note: Exact Multan records: multan 900–1000 and multan-1783 1783–1800, both circa and generated from historical basemaps.

sources.title: Human History Map imported summaries
sources.note: Byte-identical imported modern-city summaries for both ids; identity clue only, not independent historical authority.

sources.title: Human History Map research coverage registry
sources.note: One exact feature and one missing card per target; identity, chronology, and borders previously unreviewed.

sources.title: Human History Map 800 borders
sources.note: Pre-start control for the medieval atlas feature and fixed point owners.

sources.title: Human History Map 900 borders
sources.note: Sole multan feature, decoded geometry, probes, shared arcs, and the failure to contain Multan city.

sources.title: Human History Map 1000 borders
sources.note: Medieval endpoint seam; atlas assigns Multan city and the target polygon area to broad replacement features.

sources.title: Human History Map 1715 borders
sources.note: Late pre-start control assigning the Multan region to the imported Mughal Empire feature.

sources.title: Human History Map 1783 borders
sources.note: Sole multan-1783 feature, decoded geometry, probes, shared arcs, and oversized southwest-Punjab envelope.

sources.title: Human History Map 1800 borders
sources.note: Late endpoint seam repainting Multan as Sikh eighteen years before the documented 1818 conquest.

sources.title: Human History Map 1815 borders
sources.note: Post-end control bizarrely assigning Multan probes to a Maratha feature before the 1818 Sikh conquest.

sources.title: Constructing Islam on the Indus: sample chapter
sources.note: Cambridge University Press discussion of tenth-century Ismaili Multan, uncertain foundation dating, and later Ghaznavid invasions.

sources.title: Catalogue of Sikh Coins in the British Museum
sources.note: British Museum catalogue record and associated history for Multan’s 1772–79 Sikh occupation, 1779 Durrani recovery, commerce, minting, and 1818 conquest.

sources.title: Changing Dynamics of Arab Rule in Multan from the Eighth to Eleventh Centuries CE
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Islamic Studies article on Banu Samah rule, mercantile cosmopolitanism, religious plurality, pilgrimage economy, and Fatimid transition.

sources.title: The Mediaeval Ismailis of the Iranian Lands
sources.note: Institute of Ismaili Studies chronology for a Fatimid-aligned principality around 958 and Mahmud’s 1005 intervention.

sources.title: Bilingual Coins of Sulayman: A Samid Amir of Medieval Multan
sources.note: Journal of the Oriental Numismatic Society study of silver dammas, proto-Sharada and Kufic legends, titles, weights, and regional exchange.

sources.title: Silver coin of Munabbih, Amir of Multan
sources.note: British Museum object record for a 0.50-gram Multan silver coin, 800–1000, with Nagari and Kufic inscriptions and Varaha title.

sources.title: Fatimid silver coin of al-Aziz minted at Multan
sources.note: British Museum object record for an eight-millimetre, 0.55-gram Kufic coin minted at Multan, 975–996.

sources.title: Multan religious evidence, 950–1000
sources.note: Humboldt University DAMAST evidence registry tied to al-Muqaddasi and modern reference works for mosque, temple, Islam, Hinduism, and Shiism.

sources.title: al-Muqaddasi, Ahsan al-taqasim: scholarly editions
sources.note: Brill machine-readable scholarly editions of al-Muqaddasi’s late tenth-century Arabic geography.

sources.title: Kitab ahsan al-taqasim fi marifat al-aqalim
sources.note: NYU/Columbia digitized 1906 Arabic edition used to bound what the geographic account does and does not document.

sources.title: Multan
sources.note: Scholarly Turkish Diyanet encyclopedia synthesis of Istakhri, Ibn Hawqal, al-Muqaddasi, Fatimid allegiance, commerce, and later political chronology.

sources.title: Multan, the city of Saints
sources.note: Bahauddin Zakariya University institutional overview naming early visitors and the city’s long role in learning, culture, riverine agriculture, and travel.

sources.title: History of Multan: Some Reflections
sources.note: Bahauddin Zakariya University journal record for the city’s geographic, cultural, and historical importance and limits of early archaeology.

sources.title: Coins of Arab Sind and Multan
sources.note: Ancient Pakistan article by British Museum curator Robert Bracey on unpublished and previously catalogued Arab Sind and Multan coinage.

sources.title: Murad’s travels: courtesanly mobility, honour, and defiance in late eighteenth-century Multan
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of the 1806–07 Persian Jaur-o-Jafa manuscript and the late eighteenth-century setting, performance world, family, gender, mobility, and legal power.

sources.title: Jaur-o-Jafa manuscript excerpts and figures: supplementary material
sources.note: Cambridge supplementary material with manuscript excerpts and paintings showing performers, horses, camels, correspondence, and travel.

sources.title: Our History: Multan
sources.note: Government of Punjab district history for broad local chronology, Mughal and Durrani phases, Muzaffar Khan, and 1818 capture; used cautiously.

sources.title: District History: Muzaffargarh
sources.note: Government of Punjab record that Muzaffargarh was founded and fortified by Multan governor Muzaffar Khan in 1794.

sources.title: Multan: Phases of Urban Growth
sources.note: University of the Punjab urban-geography study of the citadel mound, walled city, old riverbed, narrow specialized bazaars, and 1757 mosque-shop complex.

sources.title: Tomb of Shah Rukn-e-Alam, Multan
sources.note: UNESCO tentative-list record for the 1320–24 octagonal tomb, brickwork, timber reinforcement, glazing, and architectural significance.

sources.title: Eighteenth-century tile attributed to Multan
sources.note: Metropolitan Museum object record for a large molded and glazed earthenware tile attributed to eighteenth-century Multan.

sources.title: Hazrat Bahauddin Zakariya, Multan
sources.note: Punjab Auqaf institutional record for Zakariya’s thirteenth-century Multan career, mausoleum plan, and later shrine continuity.

sources.title: Multan silver coin of the Sikh Misal period
sources.note: British Museum object identifier for a silver coin minted at Multan in 1779, the closing year of the first Sikh occupation.

sources.title: Sovereignty, Space, and Identity: The Politics of Power in Eighteenth-Century Punjab
sources.note: Harvard dissertation on Iranian, Afghan, Sikh, and local sovereignty, social actors, space, and identity in eighteenth-century Punjab.

sources.title: Punjab: A History from Aurangzeb to Mountbatten
sources.note: Scholarly regional history hosted by Ziauddin University Library, including the 1818 siege, fort, Muzaffar Khan, his family, and post-conquest violence.

sources.title: Boundaries of Afghanistan
sources.note: Encyclopaedia Iranica chronology identifying the loss of Multan to Sikh expansion in 1818.
